docs.title: Time Series Forecasting
docs.text: A forecasting system for energy assets with multi-layer analysis and flexibility optimization.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run ipython

See Architecture for the system design.

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text:
This project implements a layered forecasting approach:

  1. Raw metering data
  2. Point forecasts with uncertainty
  3. Derived features (daily energy, peaks, ramps)
  4. Asset profiling and behavior classification
  5. Anomaly detection
  6. Flexibility forecasting
  7. Portfolio aggregation
  8. Trading optimization

docs.title: Layered Progression
docs.text:
Metering Data
    |
    v
Point Forecasts + Uncertainty
    |
    +---> Daily Energy
    +---> Peak/Ramp Rates
    +---> Asset Profiles
    |
    v
Anomaly Detection
    |
    v
Flexibility Envelope
    |
    v
Portfolio Aggregation
    |
    v
Optimization & Trading

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
1. Forecast as intermediate layer: Not a final output, but input to downstream analysis
  2. Uncertainty-driven: Always include prediction intervals, not just point estimates
  3. Asset profiling: Classify assets by behavioral fingerprints
  4. Swappable models: Standard forecast contract enables model replacement
  5. Portfolio view: Leverage correlation and aggregation benefits

docs.title: Standard Forecast Contract
docs.text:
All forecasts use a consistent schema:

{
    "asset_id": str,           # Unique asset identifier
    "timestamp": datetime,     # Forecast target time
    "yhat": float,            # Point forecast
    "lower": float,           # Lower prediction interval
    "upper": float,           # Upper prediction interval
    "model_version": str,     # Which model produced this
    "forecast_ts": datetime   # When forecast was made
}

docs.title: Creating a New Notebook
docs.text:
uv run marimo edit new_topic_exploration.md

Follow this structure:

  2. Hypotheses or questions being explored

  4. Analysis with visualizations
  5. Findings section summarizing conclusions

When validated, create a markdown file in docs/findings/ linking back to the notebook.

docs.title: MkDocs Documentation Setup
docs.text: How the documentation site is built and deployed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This project uses MkDocs with Material theme to generate a documentation site published on GitHub Pages.

  • Source: docs_src/ (markdown files)
  • Built output: docs/ (HTML, CSS, JS)
  • Published: https://rhyslwells.github.io/time-series-project
  • Deployment: Automatic via GitHub Actions

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
project/
├── docs_src/                    Source markdown files
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── architecture.md
│   ├── findings/
│   ├── methodology/
│   ├── data/
│   ├── notebooks.md
│   └── coding/
│
├── docs/                        Built HTML (auto-generated)
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── assets/
│   └── [all built files]
│
├── mkdocs.yml                   MkDocs configuration
└── .github/workflows/deploy.yml Auto-build workflow

docs.title: 1. You Edit Source Files
docs.text:
Edit markdown files in docs_src/:

# Edit any markdown file
vim docs_src/findings/my_finding.md

docs.title: 2. Commit and Push
docs.text:
git add docs_src/
git commit -m "Document new finding"
git push origin main

docs.title: 3. GitHub Actions Builds Automatically
docs.text: The workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml): - Triggers on push to main branch - Installs mkdocs and Material theme - Builds from docs_src/ to docs/ - Commits built files back to repo - Pushes to main

docs.title: 4. GitHub Pages Deploys
docs.text:
GitHub Pages automatically serves the latest docs/ folder at: 

https://rhyslwells.github.io/time-series-project

No manual steps needed. Just edit, commit, push.

docs.title: Building Locally
docs.text:
To test changes before pushing:

# Install dependencies (if not already done)
uv sync --all-extras

# Build the site
uv run mkdocs build

# Or serve with live reload
uv run mkdocs serve

Then visit http://localhost:8000

docs.title: mkdocs.yml
docs.text:
Key settings:

site_name: Time Series Forecasting
docs_dir: docs_src           # Read markdown from here
site_dir: docs               # Build to here
theme:
  name: material             # Material design theme

nav:                          # Navigation structure
  - Home: index.md
  - Findings: findings/index.md
  - etc...

docs.title: GitHub Actions Workflow
docs.text:
File: .github/workflows/deploy.yml

Triggers on: - Push to main branch - Changes to docs_src/** or mkdocs.yml

Does: 1. Checkout code 2. Install Python 3.10 3. Install mkdocs and mkdocs-material 4. Run mkdocs build (reads docs_src/, writes docs/) 5. Commit and push docs/ folder

docs.title: Do NOT Manually Edit docs/
docs.text:
The docs/ folder is auto-generated. Any manual changes will be overwritten on the next build.

Edit docs_src/ instead.

docs.title: Adding New Pages
docs.text:
1. Create markdown file in docs_src/: 

    # Example: new finding
touch docs_src/findings/new_discovery.md

  2. Add to navigation in mkdocs.yml: 

    nav:
  - Findings:
      - findings/index.md
      - New Discovery: findings/new_discovery.md

  3. Write content, commit, push: 

    git add docs_src/
git commit -m "Add new discovery page"
git push

  4. Workflow auto-builds → site updates in ~1-2 minutes

docs.title: Linking Between Pages
docs.text:
Use relative markdown links:

# From findings/my_finding.md to methodology page
See [Model Selection](../methodology/model_selection.md)

# From docs_src root to marimo notebook in repo root
Explore the [investigation](../asset_profiling_exploration.md)

docs.title: Build fails: "unknown field python-version"
docs.text: Your pyproject.toml has invalid [tool.uv] config. Remove it—requires-python in [project] is sufficient.

docs.title: Links show as broken in built site
docs.text: Check that: - File path is correct - Using relative links from the markdown file location - File exists in docs_src/

docs.title: Site doesn't update after push
docs.text: Check GitHub Actions: 1. Go to repo → Actions tab 2. Look for "Deploy Docs" workflow 3. Check if it passed or failed 4. Logs show what went wrong

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Installed via pyproject.toml:

mkdocs>=1.5.0
mkdocs-material>=9.0.0

Install with: 

uv sync --all-extras

docs.title: Important: MkDocs 2.0 Breaking Changes
docs.text:
MkDocs 2.0 (currently in development) will introduce backward-incompatible changes:

  • Plugin system will be removed
  • Theme overrides will break
  • No migration path for existing projects
  • Material for MkDocs will not be compatible

Action needed: Before MkDocs 2.0 is released, we need to either: 1. Lock to MkDocs 1.x 2. Migrate to a different documentation tool 3. Wait for Material for MkDocs to release a 2.0-compatible version

Currently using MkDocs 1.5.x, so there's time to plan. Monitor: - https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Assets can be classified into behavioral clusters based on time series characteristics. This enables targeted forecasting strategies per asset type.

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
1. Assets split into 3-4 distinct behavioral clusters
  2. Cluster membership predicts optimal forecast model
  3. Seasonality strength is the primary discriminator
  4. Intermittency and autocorrelation further refine classification

docs.title: Characteristics Analyzed
docs.text:
• Mean load
  • Variance and coefficient of variation
  • Seasonality strength (seasonal subseries decomposition)
  • Autocorrelation (ACF lag-1)
  • Intermittency ratio (% near-zero values)
  • Peak-to-average ratio
  • Ramp frequency and magnitude

docs.title: Clusters Identified
docs.text: Cluster Name Characteristics Best Model A Stable Low variance, high seasonality SARIMA B Variable High variance, weak seasonality GBDT C Intermittent Low mean, many zeros, sporadic Quantile Regression

docs.text:

  • Test model-to-cluster mapping in production
  • Monitor cluster membership changes
  • Develop adaptive model selection

docs.title: Why Standard Forecast Contract?
docs.text:
• Problem: Different models output different schemas
  • Solution: Standardize on (asset_id, timestamp, yhat, lower, upper, model_version)
  • Benefit: Models become swappable without downstream changes

docs.title: Why Asset Profiling First?
docs.text:
• Problem: Single model doesn't work for all assets
  • Solution: Classify assets, use targeted models per class
  • Benefit: Better accuracy, clearer model assignment logic

docs.title: Why Prediction Intervals Over Point Forecasts?
docs.text:
• Problem: Users need to know forecast reliability
  • Solution: Always provide lower and upper bounds
  • Benefit: Enables risk-aware decision making in optimization
